stories.headline: Trump takes on Somali welfare dependency in Thanksgiving message, lays out who should stay in US
stories.note: Trump used his Thanksgiving message to hammer welfare dependency and fraud in Minnesota, a fight that keeps Democrats on defense.
body: President Trump posted a long Thanksgiving message on Truth Social on Thursday that mixed holiday thanks for "AMERICAN PATRIOTS" with sharp words for the "Radical Far Left" and for Minnesota's Somali community, which he has repeatedly accused of public-assistance fraud.

Trump thanked what he called the small share of Somali residents who work without government aid, saying they should be allowed to stay, while arguing those who are jobless and on benefits should be removed right away to save Minnesota.
He also said the violent criminals he claims entered the country illegally have largely been deported, sending them a sarcastic holiday greeting and vowing that "you will never be back."
DNC Chair Ken Martin, a Minnesotan, fired back on X, accusing Trump of "spewing hatred" on the holiday and defending Somali Americans as business owners, teachers and health care workers.

Fox notes that Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, cited data at a January Oversight hearing showing 54% of Somali-headed households in Minnesota receive food stamps. Secretary of State Marco Rubio shared his own holiday video celebrating American opportunity.
Why it matters: Welfare fraud in Minnesota has become a signature GOP issue, and Trump is making sure Democrats have to answer for it even on a holiday.

stories.headline: Universities, schools nationwide use Thanksgiving as chance to promote 'Day of Mourning' and decolonization
stories.note: Campuses and school districts recasting Thanksgiving as a 'Day of Mourning' hands Republicans a ready-made culture-war example.
body: A Fox News Digital review found a number of colleges and K-12 systems using Thanksgiving to push counter-programming about colonialism, mourning and "decolonization."

George Washington University held a Nov. 18 event examining Thanksgiving, Christmas and Independence Day through an intersectional lens, and UW-Milwaukee hosted an "AlterNative Giving" gathering offered as an alternative to the traditional story.

Salem State University promoted the holiday as a "National Day of Mourning" and told students its campus sits on land taken from the Massachusett tribe. Occidental College called it a reminder of settler colonialism, while Pratt Institute and the University at Albany list the day as a National Day of Mourning on their calendars.

The trend reaches younger kids too: a Loudoun County, Virginia, parent pushed back on lessons teaching children Thanksgiving is a day of mourning, and Oregon's Bethel School District links to a "Decolonizing Thanksgiving" toolkit on its equity page.
Why it matters: Parents' rights and patriotic education were winning issues for Republicans, and stories like this keep the spotlight on what left-leaning schools are teaching.

stories.headline: From Hollywood mogul to Biden-Harris insiders, Democrats turn to familiar faces to shape their next chapter
stories.note: Incoming Democratic governors are stocking transitions with Biden-era retreads and a Hollywood mogul facing misconduct lawsuits.
body: After their midterm gains, incoming Democratic leaders are filling their transition teams with former Biden administration officials, business executives and entertainment figures, Fox News Digital reports.

New Mexico Gov.-elect Deb Haaland picked a former Biden speechwriter and an ex-Interior official, California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra chose his former senior counselor from Biden's HHS to run transition policy, and Ohio Gov.-elect Amy Acton named a former Biden aide as a co-chair.

In Georgia, Gov.-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms added Tyler Perry to her team, drawing criticism because Perry faces two active lawsuits alleging sexual assault and misconduct. Perry has denied the allegations. Bottoms previously worked as an executive producer on a Netflix sitcom made by his studio.

Elsewhere, Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson's team includes lawyers who pursued outgoing AG Ken Paxton, and Wisconsin Gov.-elect David Crowley tapped former Milwaukee Bucks executive Alex Lasry. Most campaigns did not respond to Fox's requests for comment.
Why it matters: Leaning on Biden-era insiders and celebrity donors gives Republicans an easy argument that the 'new' Democrats are the same old crowd.

stories.headline: Incoming NJ Dem congressman once worked at al Qaeda front group — now he's speaking at alleged Hamas-tied confab
stories.note: A newly elected House Democrat's ties to groups accused of terror links give the GOP fresh ammunition on the party's radical wing.
body: Incoming New Jersey Democratic Rep. Adam Hamawy is set to speak twice this weekend at the annual Palestine Convention run by American Muslims for Palestine, a group that has faced congressional probes and a civil lawsuit over alleged Hamas ties, the New York Post reports.

The Post says Hamawy once worked at a nonprofit that served as a front for al Qaeda in the 1990s, and the paper previously reported he testified as a witness for the "Blind Sheikh," Omar Abdel-Rahman, at a 1995 trial.

In 2025, Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., opened an investigation into AMP's leadership over alleged links to Hamas. Hamawy's panels will include AMP executive director Osama Abuirshaid, whom Cassidy flagged over past interviews with Hamas leaders.

Linda Sarsour and former Rep. Cori Bush are also on the speaker list. Representatives for Hamawy and AMP did not immediately respond to the Post. Hamawy, an Egyptian-born surgeon and Army veteran, easily won the seat held by retiring Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman.
Why it matters: Republicans can point to Hamawy as a sign of where the incoming Democratic caucus is heading before he is even sworn in.

stories.headline: Read The Letter Exposing Josh Shapiro's 'Political Games' As Measles Cases Soared
stories.note: Shapiro, a top 2028 Democratic hopeful, is accused of delaying CDC help during the nation's worst measles outbreak to feud with RFK Jr.
body: Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro waited months before accepting the CDC's emergency Epi-Aid help as measles spread, and critics say his public fight with the Trump administration was the reason, The Daily Wire reports.

Pennsylvania leads the nation with more than 1,650 confirmed cases, more than a quarter of the U.S. total this year, with 571 in Lancaster County. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. said in October that Pennsylvania was the only state whose governor wouldn't accept Epi-Aid.

A September letter from the state health secretary said Pennsylvania would accept the help only if the CDC publicly counted four state-reported measles-associated deaths. The state didn't file a formal request until Oct. 7, after which a CDC officer worked on site and the state received nearly $4 million in emergency funding.

State Senate President Pro Tempore Kim Ward said the outbreak "could have been mitigated sooner" had Shapiro taken the help "instead of fighting for the sake of headlines." An HHS spokeswoman also accused him of politicizing the crisis. Shapiro didn't respond; his health department credited its own staff for falling case counts.
Why it matters: Shapiro is one of the Democrats' leading 2028 names, and a charge that he put politics ahead of public health could follow him.

stories.headline: Tim Walz Refuses To Pardon Thanksgiving Turkey
stories.note: A lighthearted send-off for outgoing Gov. Walz that also revisits his rocky record, from the 2020 riots to the feeding-program fraud.
body: In one of his final acts as Minnesota governor, Tim Walz "presented" a 36-pound turkey named Gary at the state capitol on Tuesday instead of pardoning it, and the bird is headed to the grocery store, The Daily Wire reports.

Minnesota governors have followed this no-pardon tradition since the early 2000s. "Minnesotans know turkeys are delicious too," Walz said, standing alongside the state agriculture commissioner and turkey growers.
Minnesota is the nation's top turkey producer, raising about 34 million birds this year. President Trump, meanwhile, pardoned two turkeys, Freedom and Feathers, at the White House the same day.

The article notes that Walz made headlines earlier this year for pardoning a Laotian illegal immigrant convicted of sexually assaulting a child, who was later deported by the Trump administration. Walz is not running again and will be succeeded by Sen. Amy Klobuchar in January.
Why it matters: Walz leaves office with the Floyd riots and massive fraud scandals on his record, a legacy Republicans will keep tying to Minnesota Democrats.

stories.headline: Dark Eagle, America's first operational long-range hypersonic missile battery, is 'ready to go,' Army honcho claims
stories.note: The Army's first hypersonic missile battery is finally fielded under Trump after years of Biden-era delays.
body: After a three-year delay, the Army's first long-range hypersonic weapon battery, called Dark Eagle, is now fully fielded and operational, Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano told Breaking Defense, according to the New York Post.
"It is fully fielded. It is ready to go," Lozano said, calling it a globally deployable warfighting capability.

The system is designed to launch a missile flying about 3,800 mph and hitting targets as far as 1,725 miles away. The Army originally aimed to field it in 2023 but ran into engineering setbacks, and missed a later target date as well. It is unclear exactly when it became fully fielded.

Experts have long warned that Russia and China led the U.S. in hypersonics, a gap Secretary of War Pete Hegseth has blamed on the Biden administration. The Army is now working on second and third batteries, though Lozano gave no timeline.
Why it matters: Closing the hypersonic gap with China and Russia is a national-security win the Trump administration can claim as its own.
